findings.title: Escape can advance due ticks before pausing
findings.claim: A frame that receives Escape pumps due simulation ticks before it sets the user pause reason. After a delayed frame, the ship can advance many ticks even though the player has pressed pause.
findings.why: The driver can process up to 120 due ticks in that pump, making pause visibly late after a stall. The pause test does not cover an Escape edge with ticks due at frame entry.
findings.fix: Apply the Escape edges and sync the pause state before `driver.pump()`, then compute alpha after the pump. Add a headless test with due ticks queued when Escape is sampled.

findings.title: Wheel remainder survives an idle gap without render frames
findings.claim: When the next sampled frame contains wheel input, the runtime updates `lastWheelAt` before checking the idle interval, so an old fractional delta can combine with a new scroll after more than 200 ms without rendered frames.
findings.why: A resumed view can zoom an extra notch. The existing test covers an idle interval with an intervening render frame, which clears the remainder.
findings.fix: Check elapsed time and clear `wheelAcc` before recording the new wheel timestamp. Test the first wheel sample after a gap with no intervening `frame()` call.
